scope: JoyAI direct RV2V late flower-contact prompt enhancement and full-timeline Best-of-4 noise selection
summary: A frozen persistent-contact prompt and full-stream seeds 17, 42, 73, and 101 improved late projected contact from the prior direct JoyAI result's 5/11 to 9/11 for every candidate. Seeds 17 and 42 tied at 146/147 persistent-grasp frames on H.264 screening; independent self-flow jitter selected seed 17. Its authoritative FFV1 audit measured 9/11 late contact and 145/147 persistent-grasp frames, so the result and side-by-side comparison remain PARTIAL rather than promoted.
lessons: Explicit prompt constraints materially improved late image-space contact, but all four noise seeds shared the same two late misses, indicating a systematic model or conditioning limitation rather than a seed-only failure.
H.264 screening can fill single-pixel contact gaps; the FFV1 audit is authoritative and must be retained even when its persistent-grasp recall is lower.
Temporal tie-breaking must use independent self-flow measurements for each candidate; cross-seed optical-flow comparison confounds appearance differences with jitter.
limitations: No candidate reached the frozen 1.0 late-contact and persistent-grasp hard gates; seed 17 failed late frames 627-628 and persistent-grasp frames 574 and 637 in the lossless audit.
The remaining late spatial-chroma gate also failed under historical frozen limits.
All measurements are 2-D image-space diagnostics on one scene, with no metric depth, force closure, sensor contact, or real-robot evidence.
next_actions: Run a new predeclared experiment that targets the systematic final-release/contact interval rather than expanding the current seed pool after observing results.
Require the new challenger to pass 11/11 late projected contact and 147/147 lossless persistent grasp without regressing flower identity, robot topology, temporal jitter, or adversarial detection.
